title: Network & configuration check
intro: Checks your public address, NAT, clock, ports 80/443, DDNS resolution and certificate validity. It queries the public IP lookup services configured for DDNS.

r.publicIPv4Fail: Could not determine the public IPv4 address
r.direct: This machine holds the public address {ip} directly
r.behindNat: Behind NAT: this machine only has a private address
r.cgnat: A carrier-grade NAT address ({ip}) was found on a network interface
r.clockUnknown: Could not measure the clock offset
r.port80Denied: No permission to listen on port 80
r.port443Denied: No permission to listen on port 443
r.direct6: This machine holds the public IPv6 address {ip} directly

h.publicIPv4Fail: Check outbound connectivity and DNS, or change the IP lookup URLs in the DDNS settings.
h.behindNat: Inbound access needs port forwarding on the router, UPnP, STUN, IPv6 or a tunnel (Tailscale, frp, Cloudflare Tunnel).
h.cgnat: Your ISP may not give you a public IPv4 address. Use IPv6, STUN or a tunnel. Note that Tailscale also uses the 100.64.0.0/10 range.
h.clockSkew: A wrong clock breaks two-step verification codes and certificate validation. Enable NTP time sync.
h.portInUse: Normal if a Web Service listener of Gately uses it. Otherwise find the other program with ss -ltnp.
h.portDenied: Run as root, grant CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, or listen on a higher port and forward to it.
h.ddnsMismatch: DNS caches may take a few minutes to refresh. If it persists, check the DDNS task log.
h.ddnsUnresolved: Create the record at your DNS provider or check the DDNS task log.
h.certExpiring: Check the certificate renewal log; make sure DNS credentials or port 80 are reachable.
h.certExpired: Renew the certificate now from the SSL page and check the renewal log.
h.direct6: Services on this machine are reachable over IPv6 without port forwarding, as long as the router and local firewall allow the ports.
